help.title: Sitemap – Help
help.intro: The sitemap provides a graphical overview of the structure of the app in the form of a tree structure. It lists all configured menus, pages and sections and shows their dependencies. From the main menu through submenus and pages down to the individual sections. Each node has a type, which is indicated by color and label.

main.label: Main menu
main.content: The root of the navigation. It bundles the top-level menu entries and is automatically expanded when opened.

sub.label: Submenu
sub.content: An expandable entry that groups further menu entries (displayed as an accordion in the menu).

navigate.label: Navigate
navigate.content: Leads to an internal page of the app. The linked page is shown in the tree as a child node.

browse.label: Browse
browse.content: Opens an external address (URL) in a new tab.

context.label: Context menu
context.content: The menu at the top right of the page with additional actions that affect all displayed data.

call.label: Action
call.content: Triggers a function or command without navigating (e.g. upload file).

divider.label: Divider
divider.content: A purely visual dividing line to structure the menu – without function. Also used as a placeholder for functions not yet implemented.

page.label: Page
page.content: A CMS page consisting of an ordered list of sections.

section.label: Section
section.content: A single content block within a page (e.g. article, gallery, map, calendar).

usage.title: How to use the sitemap:
usage.expand: Click on the arrow symbol to expand or collapse a node and display its child elements.
usage.label: For each node, the translated menu text is shown; above it, in smaller type, is the technical name of the entry.
usage.edit: Hover over a node and click on the pencil symbol to edit the associated menu, page or section directly.
usage.export: Via the menu at the top right you can export the structure as a table (raw) or as sitemap XML.
usage.roles: The displayed roles are also important. They determine who can see the respective entry. You can change the role by clicking on the pencil symbol.

welcome.bannerAltText: Background image with a rower on Lake Zurich.

notfound.subTitle: This is a dead end.
notfound.abstract: The requested HTML page could not be found. Try again with a different URL, i.e. click the menu at the top left and choose a function.
notfound.bannerAltText: Background image of the error page.

unknownpagetype.title: 404 Not Found
unknownpagetype.subTitle: This is a dead end.
unknownpagetype.abstract: An HTML page with an unknown type was called. Please try again with a different URL, i.e. click the menu at the top left and choose a function.
unknownpagetype.bannerAltText: Background image of the error page.

content_state.label: Status
content_state.helper: The status helps the content creators during creation. For example, new pages can be shown to only a few users while in draft or during a review.

accordion.label: Accordion
accordion.description: An accordion (GUI) is a graphical user interface element that expands and collapses stacked content areas by clicking on a heading. It serves to organize large amounts of information, such as in FAQ areas, in a space-saving way by showing only the relevant content while other areas remain compact.

album.label: Album
album.description: An album shows an overview of a number of photos.

blog.label: Blog
blog.description: A blog (short for weblog) is a regularly updated, usually chronologically ordered online diary or journal on a website. It serves to share content such as texts, photos or videos on specific topics, often from the subjective point of view of the author (blogger). Blogs enable interaction through comments.

chat.label: Chat
chat.description: Chat overview with chat windows for direct or group communication

content.label: Content
content.description: A content page can contain any sections. It is the most general form of a page.

dashboard.label: Dashboard
dashboard.description: The dashboard gives a personalized overview of the latest news, unanswered chat messages, open tasks and upcoming appointments.

files.label: Files
files.description: This page shows files in a graphical way. It corresponds to a simple form of a file system view and consists of files and folders.

graph.label: Sitemap
graph.description: The sitemap provides a graphical overview of the structure of the app. It lists all configured menus, pages and sections and shows their dependencies.
graph.description2: The elements in this graph can be selected and edited.

landing.label: Homepage
landing.description: The main page of the website. It is usually also publicly accessible and often contains a hero section.

people.label: People
people.description: The people listed here are displayed as avatars in the section.

searchResults.label: Search results
searchResults.description: A website consisting of a search field and the search results in list form.

shop.label: Shop
shop.description: In the shop, products can be sold. Components of the shop are an overview with search, detail views of the products. In the shopping cart, the selected products are summarized with prices and released for ordering with payment.
